text:
Carlos: Thanks for the great all-hands session — dropping clarifications for infra/capacity Qs we didn't finish.
Mei: Super quick summary: APAC pilot targets SYD + BOM as staggered regions. We're focusing on predictable Reserved capacity first, then optional Burst for Hosted.
Jordan: Can you explain why BOM and SYD instead of SIN/TOK like earlier slides?
Mei: Decision based on procurement lead times + partner pricing. BOM nodes arrived sooner and SYD has better network peering for a set of customers. We'll still add SEA/JP later.
Priya: What exactly is "Burst"? Any impact on Dedicated customers?
Mei: Burst = shared spot-backed pool for Hosted. It never takes Dedicated GPU reservations. If the provider reclaims spot, autoscaler falls back per-policy.
Carlos: Fallback policy - please list exact order so customers can reason about residency and latency.
Jordan: Also include cost implications for cross-region fallback.
Mei: Fallback ordering we landed on: (1) local Reserved, (2) local Burst, (3) sibling APAC region (e.g., SYD <-> BOM), (4) EU-west if APAC exhausted, (5) US-west last resort. Cross-region egress will be displayed in Console and requires customer opt-in for automatic failover.
Priya: For customers needing strict residency, what's the API toggle?
Mei: Route config has `residency_mode` with values `preferred` (default) or `strict`. Example: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/chat/completions","region":"ap-southeast-2","residency_mode":"strict"}
```
When `strict` is set, autoscaler will queue and return 429 if capacity not available; it will never cross-region.
Carlos: Good — please add exact error header we will return so SDKs can surface it.
infra-bot: CI job started: autoscaler-playbook -> integration tests (ETA ~6m).
Jordan: How do we handle sudden PLG spikes from many small tokens? Do we scale nodes or throttle at token level?
Mei: Autoscaler has a two-tier approach: global node scaling (adds nodes/pools) and per-token soft-shaping per API key. For short spikes, tokens are shaped; for sustained need, we add Reserved capacity or burst if enabled.
Priya: If a spot-backed burst VM is reclaimed mid-inference, what do users see?
Mei: We attempt graceful drain for ~15-20s. If evicted abruptly, the request will return 502 with a trace id and be retried by the client if idempotent. We'll document recommended client retry semantics.
Carlos: Anything new on cold-start numbers in APAC? We need realistic SLAs for customers.
Mei: Cold node provisioning target <= 120s in SYD/BOM due to region quotas; warm-up/model load roughly: 7B ~ 15-25s, 13B ~ 30-45s, 70B ~ 60-90s. We'll publish median + p95 in Console.
Jordan: Billing concerns — will customers see surprise egress charges if we failover cross-region?
Mei: No surprise billing: cross-region failover requires an org-level opt-in toggle `allow_cross_region_fallback`. Console will show projected egress before enabling and we'll emit alerts once cross-region usage exceeds configurable threshold.
infra-bot: integration tests passed for autoscaler-playbook. Canary rollout queued.
Priya: Action items: (1) API: add `residency_mode` enum + error header by Fri EOD (owner: @eng-api), (2) Console: surface cross-region estimate and opt-in by next sprint (owner: @console), (3) SRE: add `region` + `model_variant` tags to cold-start telemetry (owner: @sre).
Carlos: I'll coordinate customer comms and a short FAQ "What happens if my workload hits a spot eviction?". Keep it one paragraph + link to trace-id troubleshooting.
Jordan: Minor ask: can we include a short dev-ex sample showing how to set `residency_mode` in SDKs?
Mei: Yes — DevEx will add samples for Python/Node.
infra-bot: Canary rollout started: autoscaler-playbook -> 2 regions.
Carlos: Thanks all, will post the consolidated follow-up doc in #product-update and ping teams for PR links. If anything else comes up, reply here.
infra-bot: Canary complete: autoscaler-playbook -> healthy.
